display_heading.headline: The Second Time As Farce
display_heading.deck: Travesties Repeats History In The Form Of A Diplomat's Spotty Memories Of Zurich

contact_edits.before: Jordan Pettle brings a welcome flamboyance and precision to Tzara (Jack to Henry's Algy) and David Storch's Joyce, though sometimes too muted, is fine in his prophetic utterances, as well as sporting a great cartoon outline. Oliver Dennis and Maggie Huculak are pitch perfect as the Lenins who, despite Stoppard's extensive rewrites, remain largely sealed off in their own part of the play, as in the sealed railway carriage that carried them back to Russia. Sarah Wilson and Krystin Pellerin are treats as the two young ladies, who end up butting heads and minds in a vaudeville duet ("oh, Gwendolen...oh, Cecilee") that might be even more pointed with more talking, less singing. Pellerin, as a librarian successively stern and melting, is especially fine, surpassed for endearingness only by this production's bunny, definitive in its role. - Travesties runs through March 21 at the Young Centre. Call 416-866-8666 or visit soulpepper.ca for tickets.
